probe.report:
# TLS details for onlinesbi.sbi
protocol = TLSv1.3
cipher = TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256
key_exchange_group = X25519
certificate_key = RSA 2048 bit
certificate_signature = sha256WithRSAEncryption

findings.why: TLS 1.3 suite. The key exchange is chosen separately, so make sure the X25519MLKEM768 group is enabled.
findings.replacement: TLS 1.3 with TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384 and the X25519MLKEM768 hybrid group

findings.why: ECDH key agreement is broken by Shor's algorithm, so session keys in harvested traffic can be recovered later.
findings.replacement: Hybrid X25519 + ML-KEM-768 (TLS group X25519MLKEM768)

findings.why: RSA's security rests on integer factoring, which Shor's algorithm solves in polynomial time. Recorded traffic can be decrypted after Q-Day.
findings.replacement: ML-KEM-768 (FIPS 203) for key transport; ML-DSA-65 (FIPS 204) for signatures

steps.title: Turn on hybrid post-quantum key exchange (X25519MLKEM768)
steps.why: The server negotiated a classical key exchange, so recorded sessions can be decrypted after Q-Day. Data kept 10 years + 0.25 years to migrate exceeds the 9 years to 2035.
steps.action: Upgrade the TLS terminator (OpenSSL 3.5+, or a CDN that supports it) and put X25519MLKEM768 first in the supported groups.

steps.title: Wrap long-lived records with QuantumLedger Vault
steps.why: Records kept 10 years will outlive the 2035 horizon. Backups and replicas leak too.
steps.action: Store each record under its own AES-256 key wrapped with ML-KEM-768 and signed with ML-DSA-65 (`vault.put`).

steps.title: Plan the certificate migration
steps.why: The certificate uses a classical key. Forging it needs a quantum computer at connection time, so it is not a harvest risk, but CA and browser support for PQ certificates takes years.
steps.action: Inventory certificates (the CBOM), shorten lifetimes, and track your CA's ML-DSA roadmap. Use ML-DSA now for internal PKI.

steps.title: Keep the CBOM current
steps.why: Migration is only done when the inventory says so.
steps.action: Run the readiness scanner in CI and attach the CycloneDX CBOM to each release.

plain: Uses X25519 key exchange: traffic recorded today can be decrypted by a future quantum computer.
Uses RSA 2048 certificates: breakable by a future quantum computer.
Negotiated TLS 1.3 with AES-256-GCM: the symmetric part is already strong.
